## pencil
The Pencil MCP server is the editor for .pen design files (web/mobile apps and websites). Use it to read, generate, and validate designs.

.pen files are encrypted: access them only via "pencil" MCP tools — never use Read or Grep on .pen files. Follow each tool's input schema exactly.

Always call get_app_state({ include_schema: true, include_canvas_design: true, include_scripts_and_shaders: false }) if you don't have the current .pen file schema in the context. All three flags are required. Knowing the schema is required to use any other Pencil MCP tool.

Tools: get_app_state, get_guidelines, execute, get_screenshot, export_nodes, export_html.
Also: browser.

The user is happy to batch **multiple loosely-related issues into one PR** to keep review cadence
flowing. Stated 2026-08-08 during wave 8.

**Why:** CodeRabbit gives one review per hour org-wide, so a wave of N single-issue PRs costs at
least N hours of review chain whatever order it runs in. The file-ownership graph caps how much can
run in *parallel*; the review slot caps how fast anything *lands*. Batching cuts the number of
cycles, and it is the only lever that moves the real bottleneck. See
[[project-v2-hot-file-contention-caps-parallelism]] for the other half of the constraint.

**How to apply:**

- Batch by **shared file surface first, topical relation second**. Two issues that both touch
  `facade.rs` belong together whether or not they are conceptually related, because splitting them
  guarantees a rebase. Two issues in the same subsystem that interact semantically (one changes
  where auth state comes from, the other what happens when restore fails) belong together because
  splitting them makes the second rework the first.
- 2–3 issues per PR is the working size. Do not build one giant PR: review quality drops, and
  CodeRabbit has a [[project-coderabbit-150-file-cap]].
- Give each issue its own commit inside the batch, and a `Closes #N` line per issue in the body.
- When adding scope to an agent already mid-build, tell it to finish the original issue coherently
  first and add the second on top — and to ship the first alone if the second turns out much larger
  than scoped. A blocked bug fix is worse than an extra review cycle.
- Still hold a batch behind a genuine blocker. Batching changes how work is grouped, never whether
  a dependency edge is respected.

Related: [[feedback-closes-vs-part-of-issue-hygiene]] (one `Closes` per finished issue),
[[feedback-keep-prs-draft-control-cr-timing.md]] (the orchestrator owns slot timing).

**Reaffirmed and strengthened 2026-08-19 (wave 11):** "I would like each of the PRs to close more
than one issue (if possible and appropriate)." Treat a single-issue PR as needing justification,
not as a default. This applies to slices already planned but **not yet opened** — re-batch them
mid-wave rather than waiting for the next wave.

Two things make re-batching easier than it looks mid-wave:

- A hot-file slot **frees the moment its PR merges**. The "one PR per wave per hot file" rule is
  about PRs in flight together, not the wave as a calendar unit. Once the `facade.rs` claimant
  merges, a later PR in the same wave can claim `facade.rs` — it just rebases.
- Combining is sometimes the *better review*, not merely the cheaper one. Two halves of one
  security protocol (server exchange + browser key custody) reviewed separately means no review
  ever sees the binding between them.

Related: [[project-worktree-branch-ref-goes-stale]] when re-batching into an existing branch.

Two policies the user set on 2026-08-26, after the wave-15 issue count peaked at ~167:

**1. Higher bar for a v2.0.0-milestone issue.** The v2.0.0 milestone means "must land before the
#653 staging cutover". A follow-up gets v2.0.0 ONLY if it is: a security/crypto/fail-closed or
data-loss defect; on the cutover critical path (deploy/CI/release gates); or a broken
user-visible core flow. Everything else — refactors, testkit debt, perf nits, docs niceties,
latent bugs behind unshipped surfaces, polish — goes to the `post-cutover` milestone.
Disposition order for a new finding: implement-now in the same PR > fold into an OPEN issue >
file v2.0.0 (bar above) > file post-cutover > accept-and-document in the PR body/blueprint for
trivia.

**Why:** waves were filing faster than they closed; the tracker peaked at 167 with most of wave
15 merged. The count metric must fall.

**How to apply:** brief EVERY ship/resolve/housekeeping agent with the bar; triage at filing
time, not later. A `post-cutover` milestone exists in the repo for this.

**2. Wave 16 is burndown-weighted.** Closing batches and existing-issue folds come first, new
feature slices second; fold MORE related issues per PR (the CR 1-review/hr ceiling rewards
larger, well-scoped batches). Composes with [[feedback-implement-followups-in-wave]] and
[[feedback-batch-loosely-related-issues-per-pr]].

name: feedback-batch-loosely-related-issues-per-pr
description: "Batch multiple loosely-related issues into one PR — the 1-review-per-hour CodeRabbit ceiling, not the work, is what sets wave throughput"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 2b9a962d-e9c8-4465-b4ef-93584f21a390
  modified: 2026-08-08T12:45:56.750Z
---

The user is happy to batch **multiple loosely-related issues into one PR** to keep review cadence
flowing. Stated 2026-08-08 during wave 8.

**Why:** CodeRabbit gives one review per hour org-wide, so a wave of N single-issue PRs costs at
least N hours of review chain whatever order it runs in. The file-ownership graph caps how much can
run in *parallel*; the review slot caps how fast anything *lands*. Batching cuts the number of
cycles, and it is the only lever that moves the real bottleneck. See
[[project-v2-hot-file-contention-caps-parallelism]] for the other half of the constraint.

**How to apply:**

- Batch by **shared file surface first, topical relation second**. Two issues that both touch
  `facade.rs` belong together whether or not they are conceptually related, because splitting them
  guarantees a rebase. Two issues in the same subsystem that interact semantically (one changes
  where auth state comes from, the other what happens when restore fails) belong together because
  splitting them makes the second rework the first.
- 2–3 issues per PR is the working size. Do not build one giant PR: review quality drops, and
  CodeRabbit has a [[project-coderabbit-150-file-cap]].
- Give each issue its own commit inside the batch, and a `Closes #N` line per issue in the body.
- When adding scope to an agent already mid-build, tell it to finish the original issue coherently
  first and add the second on top — and to ship the first alone if the second turns out much larger
  than scoped. A blocked bug fix is worse than an extra review cycle.
- Still hold a batch behind a genuine blocker. Batching changes how work is grouped, never whether
  a dependency edge is respected.

Related: [[feedback-closes-vs-part-of-issue-hygiene]] (one `Closes` per finished issue),
[[feedback-keep-prs-draft-control-cr-timing.md]] (the orchestrator owns slot timing).

**Reaffirmed and strengthened 2026-08-19 (wave 11):** "I would like each of the PRs to close more
than one issue (if possible and appropriate)." Treat a single-issue PR as needing justification,
not as a default. This applies to slices already planned but **not yet opened** — re-batch them
mid-wave rather than waiting for the next wave.

Two things make re-batching easier than it looks mid-wave:

- A hot-file slot **frees the moment its PR merges**. The "one PR per wave per hot file" rule is
  about PRs in flight together, not the wave as a calendar unit. Once the `facade.rs` claimant
  merges, a later PR in the same wave can claim `facade.rs` — it just rebases.
- Combining is sometimes the *better review*, not merely the cheaper one. Two halves of one
  security protocol (server exchange + browser key custody) reviewed separately means no review
  ever sees the binding between them.

Related: [[project-worktree-branch-ref-goes-stale]] when re-batching into an existing branch.

name: project-v2-hot-file-contention-caps-parallelism
description: "Engine PR parallelism is capped by a handful of hot files, not issue count — batch by file ownership"
metadata:

---

When batching v2 issues into parallel PRs, the binding constraint is hot-file contention, not the
number of actionable issues. **Re-confirmed 2026-08-07 against main `2819cb831`** after the wave-6
merges; the 2026-08-04 map drifted materially in four places.

Standing hot files:

- `crates/engine/src/facade.rs` (now 6200+, 19 of 63 commits since 1 Aug) and
  `crates/engine/tests/write_plane.rs` (now 6608) — touched by almost every engine issue
- **`crates/engine/src/net/rotation.rs` (3887 lines, 9 commits in 7 days) is now the number-one
  rotation contention point** — 8 of the 14 rotation-cluster issues edit it. It has overtaken every
  file under `rotation/`. It was not on the old map at all.
- `crates/engine/src/sync/drain.rs` (2980)
- **`crates/wasm/src/host.rs`, NOT `seams_bridge.rs`** — the old map had this backwards. host.rs took
  8 commits since 1 Aug against seams_bridge's 3.
- **New zone: the wasm↔client RPC boundary** — `packages/client/src/worker/protocol.ts` plus
  `commandCodec.ts`, `engineWasm.ts`, `engineHost.ts`, `engineClient.ts`. Six actionable issues all
  edit `protocol.ts`. Second-hottest zone after facade.rs.
- `packages/client/src/leaderRelay.ts` (596 lines, 6 commits, 5 contenders)
- Secondary: `crates/engine/src/sync/rebase.rs` (1840, 14 commits since 1 July)
- **Cooled, no longer needs an ownership zone:** `gate/floor.rs` + `seams/floor_store.rs` (606/107
  lines, 3 contenders), and `apps/web/src/engine/snapshotStore.ts` (1 contender, out of the top 25).

The #635 rotation cluster is its own contention zone — `rotation/trigger.rs` (279 lines, 3
contenders), `net/rotation.rs`, `rotation/rotate_write.rs`, `rotation/sweep.rs`,
`rotation/reseal.rs` + `rotate.rs`.

**Why:** facade.rs is 5000+ lines so different functions usually auto-merge, but signature/shape
changes ripple. The recurring failure is the semantic merge conflict in
[[project-semantic-merge-conflict-shape-change]] — two PRs both MERGEABLE that break main's compile
pairwise.

**How to apply:** batch so each PR *owns* its hot files exclusively, and sequence any PR carrying a
signature change ahead of everything touching its callers. Group small issues that collide on the
same interface into ONE PR rather than trying to parallelize them — this also conserves the
CodeRabbit quota (see [[feedback-keep-prs-draft-control-cr-timing.md]]). Reserve worktree isolation
for the batches that genuinely run concurrently.

**Re-confirm the map after every merge wave.** Closing issues retires rows, but merges also *create*
rows — and a file's contenders are not always the ones named in the issue bodies (e.g. #793 reads as
a `gate/adoption.rs` issue but also edits `rotation/reseal.rs`, colliding with a different wave).
Repo-wide sweeps like a comment-hygiene pass collide with everything; run them alone.

---
name: feedback-use-github-native-issue-dependencies
description: "Mark issue dependencies with GitHub's native blocked_by/blocking API, not prose \"Depends on\" sections"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: d6d4959d-7e94-4b31-b5a4-2baeac1e123c
  modified: 2026-08-02T20:23:42.023Z
---

Dependency edges between issues must be recorded with **GitHub's native issue-dependency
feature**, not a prose `## Depends on` / `## Blocks` section in the body.

**Why:** prose edges are error-prone. They are hand-maintained in two places, so the reverse
edge silently rots — an audit on 2026-08-02 found forward edges present and well-written on 17
recently-filed issues while **zero of seven** upstreams reciprocated. The native feature writes
both directions from a single call and surfaces in the issue UI and list filters, so it cannot
drift.

**How to apply** (the API is live on FSM1/cipher-box):

```bash
# add: issue N is blocked by issue M — pass M's DATABASE id, not its number
ID=$(env -u GITHUB_TOKEN gh api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/issues/<M> --jq '.id')
env -u GITHUB_TOKEN gh api -X POST \
  repos/FSM1/cipher-box/issues/<N>/dependencies/blocked_by -F issue_id=$ID

# read either direction
env -u GITHUB_TOKEN gh api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/issues/<N>/dependencies/blocked_by
env -u GITHUB_TOKEN gh api repos/FSM1/cipher-box/issues/<N>/dependencies/blocking
```

`issue_id` is the numeric `.id`, NOT the issue number — passing the number silently targets the
wrong issue. Posting `blocked_by` on N makes N appear under M's `blocking` automatically; never
write both sides by hand.

Keep prose only where it carries rationale the link cannot (why the dependency exists, what
specifically is inherited). Delete bare restatements of the edge itself.

Supersedes the prose half of [[feedback-followup-issues-need-dependency-edge]] — the requirement
that every deferred issue gets an immediate bidirectional edge at filing still stands, but the
mechanism is now the native API. Related: [[feedback-todos-go-to-gsd-capture-not-github-issues]],
[[feedback-closes-vs-part-of-issue-hygiene]].

name: project-gh-rest-parent-field-false-negative
description: "gh api /issues/N --jq '.parent' ALWAYS returns null — the REST payload has no parent object; every orphan check built on it is a false negative"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 8ed080ed-fffa-498c-9012-8e777bd9ef50
  modified: 2026-08-05T22:52:54.789Z
---

`env -u GITHUB_TOKEN gh api /repos/FSM1/cipher-box/issues/<N> --jq '.parent.number'` **always
returns `null`**, whether or not the issue has a parent. The REST issue payload carries no `parent`
object — the field is **`parent_issue_url`**.

So any "find the orphans" sweep written against `.parent` reports **every** issue as an orphan.
Verify parentage only via `.parent_issue_url`, or authoritatively via
`GET /repos/FSM1/cipher-box/issues/<parent>/sub_issues`. GraphQL's `parent` field does work, but
GraphQL times out on this repo often enough that REST is the usual path.

**Companion trap, same pass (2026-08-06): a track umbrella reading "0 open children" can be an
artifact of missing parentage, not completeness.** #989 (core) showed 12/12 closed and looked
ready to close — but #1050, live core-track work, was orphaned and therefore invisible in the
rollup. After parenting it read 12/13 with one open child. **Always parent the orphans BEFORE
evaluating any umbrella for closure**, never after. #990 (api) survived the same check and is
genuinely 8/8 — but note that "no open children" only proves no *tracked* work remains.

Related: [[feedback-use-github-native-issue-dependencies]] (the dependency API is keyed by the
database `id`, not the issue number — the same shape of trap one level over).

Review triage and resolution also go to the sub-agent — the sub-agent invokes the /resolve-pr-reviews skill itself, so the orchestrator context stays clear.

=== 990
# #990 api: the NestJS residual surface, registry, mailbox, and republisher track [v2.0.0]
Umbrella for every `apps/api` slice — identity auth and refresh rotation, the pin and name registry, the hosted upload path, the mailbox, the in-process republisher and record cache, the account hard-delete cascade, and the API test tiers.

The API is zero-knowledge and never serves records. Normative spec: `blueprint/api.md`.

Work is tracked as sub-issues of this one — this body carries no checkbox list.

Part of #655

=== 1526 title/body head
Two deploy-lane slices. One rewrites the staging observability surface for v2.
One binds the front's Cloudflare trust to this zone.

## deploy: rewrite the staging dashboard for v2 and re-check the Kubo caveat

**Mechanism.** The provisioned dashboard was still the v1 one. Every metric name
it queried starts with `cipherbox_`, and no such series exists anywhere in the
v2 tree. The seven provisioned alert rules were dead the same way. So the
dashboard showed "No data" in every API panel, and no alert could fire.

**What landed.**

- `docker/grafana/dashboards/cipherbox-staging.json` is rewritten over the v2
  series that `apps/api/src/ops/metrics.service.ts` actually registers. The
  `TEE Republishing` row is deleted: v2 has no TEE, and the republisher is a
  keyless re-PUT module inside the API.
- New rows cover the republisher inventory walk and re-PUT counts, mailbox
  depth and cap rejections, auth attempts and throttle rejections, and the
  read-accelerator gate.
- `docker/grafana/alerts/` gets its v2 disposition: five v1 rules retire, two
  are ported to v2 series, and two new rules land.
- `docker/alloy-config.river` pins the `job` label and corrects the keep-list.
- `docker/MONITORING.md` is brought back in step with the code.

**Upstream health.** The `forward_auth` deny-on-any-non-204 obligation means an
upstream-down condition on the two gated vhosts reaches no Caddy error line —
both vhosts discard their logs. Metrics are the only signal. So `up` now
survives the keep-list, the accelerator row plots it, and a new rule fires when
either accelerator stays down.

**The Kubo caveat, re-checked.** The caveat said Kubo emitted no libp2p metrics.
That held on v0.34. Staging runs `ipfs/kubo:v0.42.0` today. I ran that exact
image and read `/debug/metrics/prometheus`: it exports 197 metric families,
including the full `libp2p_*` set. The caveat is retired.

One correction came out of the same probe. `libp2p_network_in_bytes_total` and
`libp2p_network_out_bytes_total` — which both the v1 dashboard and the old
Alloy keep-list named — do not exist in v0.42.0 at all. Bandwidth now comes
from `process_network_receive_bytes_total` and its transmit counterpart, which
the probe confirms. `ghcr.io/ipfs/someguy:v0.11.1` was probed the same way.

The staging VPS has 2 vCPU and the Grafana Cloud tier is small, so the keep-list
stays tight: no kubo histogram families, and the two dead names are removed
rather than joined by more.

Closes #1395.

## deploy: authenticate Cloudflare to this zone, not to Cloudflare at large

**Mechanism.** `trusted_proxies` carries Cloudflare's published ranges. Those
ranges are shared infrastructure. Any Cloudflare tenant can point a proxied
record at the staging origin address, override the origin `Host` so Caddy routes
to a fronted vhost, and arrive from inside a trusted range. The front then
treats an unauthenticated proxy as trusted, which is the premise every IP-keyed
limit below it rests on.

**What landed.** A new `(origin_tls)` snippet in `docker/Caddyfile` replaces the
three repeated `tls` lines. It adds:

## ISSUE #1366 — a held drain op blocks every queued content version

**Verdict: VALID (STALE — not touched by wave-16 PR #1524).**

**The refusal, and that it is correctly per-node in isolation.** `refuse_unpaired_version` (facade.rs:7043-7058, same as above) checks `staged_version_cid(node)` (facade.rs:7062-7069), which filters `pending_ops()` by `op.target == node` — this check itself is per-node and correct on its own.

**The drain queue is a single global gate, not per-target.** `BlockedOp` (crates/engine/src/sync/drain.rs:357-364) and `SettingsHold` (drain.rs:372-380) are each held in a single-slot `RefCell<Option<...>>`: `blocked: &'a RefCell<Option<BlockedOp>>` (drain.rs:432) and `settings_hold: &'a RefCell<Option<SettingsHold>>` (drain.rs:436) — one cell per drain session, not one per node.

`pass()` (drain.rs:698-761) gates the **entire** tick on these two cells before touching any op:
```
if !self.quota_admits_the_held_head(queued).await { return Ok(()); }   // drain.rs:705-707
if !self.settings_admit_the_held_head(queued) { return Ok(()); }        // drain.rs:708-710
```
`quota_admits_the_held_head` (drain.rs:881-907) and `settings_admit_the_held_head` (drain.rs:915-927) only check whether the held op is `still_queued` and whether the condition that caused the hold (quota room, or the same settings refusal) has cleared — neither checks whether the *current* op being considered targets the same node as the held one. So while a hold is active, `pass()` returns before reaching `rebased.applied`/`dead_letters` processing for **any** op, regardless of target node. Any node with a still-queued, not-yet-published version stays `ContentUnavailable` for as long as the hold persists — this is exactly the claim in the issue.

The hold is set from `apply_valve` (drain.rs:763-876): `Halt::Blocked { needed_bytes }` sets `self.blocked` (drain.rs:859-865), `Halt::HeldBySettings(refusal)` sets `self.settings_hold` (drain.rs:867-874). Each of the two arms clears the other (comment at drain.rs:856-858: "One pass raises one halt... rather than leaving two cells claiming the same head").

**No error carries op-id or cause.** `EngineError::ContentUnavailable { message: String }` (facade.rs:1119-1126) carries only a free-text message. `BlockedOp`/`SettingsHold` carry `op_id`/`node`/`needed_bytes` or `refusal` internally, but that structured data does not reach the read-path error — a caller sees an opaque string, never learns it was a held drain op rather than an ordinary unpublished-version wait.

**Blueprint law.** blueprint/engine.md:392 states replay is "FIFO in performed order through the standard rebase" — confirms strict FIFO is intentional in general. But the blueprint explicitly rejects unbounded head-of-line stall for one related class of failure: blueprint/engine.md:726-730, on dual placement legs — "Under strict-FIFO stop-at-first-failure a both-must-succeed rule would let an offline home node stall every later mutation in the vault, so the op completes once hosted succeeds and external has either succeeded or exhausted its attempts." That principle (do not let one leg's failure stall the whole vault) was applied to placement legs but was never extended to `BlockedOp`/`SettingsHold`, which still block the whole queue. No blueprint sentence anywhere authorizes per-node bypass of a quota/settings hold, so the current single-slot design is not a documented law being violated by a bug — it is simply an unaddressed gap.

**PR #1524 (aa58d7853, "unfreeze an unpreservable dead letter...") did not touch this.** `git log --oneline -20 -- crates/engine/src/sync/drain.rs` shows aa58d7853 as the second-most-recent commit touching drain.rs. Its diff (confirmed by inspection) adds `Preservation::Refused`/`Preservation::Kept` handling, a new `Halt::Permanent(DeadLetterReason::AlreadyPublished)` arm, and `release_if_refused` — all about dead-letter classification, replayed-create detection, and reclaim-stall reporting. It never touches `blocked`, `settings_hold`, `quota_admits_the_held_head`, or `settings_admit_the_held_head`. The most recent drain.rs commit, eee8ce604 ("key the held set by plane and renew the scope pointer"), is also unrelated — its "held set" is `HeldRecords`/`HeldKey` in crates/engine/src/net/liveness.rs:94-153, the record-plane republish/renewal lease tracker, a completely different structure from `BlockedOp`/`SettingsHold`. Neither PR changes head-of-line behavior for the drain queue.

**File list:** crates/engine/src/sync/drain.rs (the `pass()` gate, `BlockedOp`/`SettingsHold` storage, `apply_valve`), crates/engine/src/facade.rs (surface op-id/cause on `ContentUnavailable`, and/or expose which node is held so a caller can distinguish "my version is held" from "someone else's is").

**Estimate: L (2-3 days).** Fixing this correctly means re-deriving per-target admission (skip ops targeting a node different from the held one, without breaking the FIFO-rebase ordering guarantee the blueprint states at line 392) plus threading a cause/op-id through to `ContentUnavailable` — a bigger design change than #1361, and it risks interacting with the same rebase/apply loop `pass()` already carefully orders.

`pass()` (drain.rs:698-761) gates the **entire** tick on these two cells before touching any op:
```

if !self.settings_admit_the_held_head(queued) { return Ok(()); }        // drain.rs:708-710
```

Both issues touch **crates/engine/src/facade.rs** (the `ContentUnavailable` refusal sites and `refuse_unpaired_version`). #1366 also touches **crates/engine/src/sync/drain.rs**, which #1361 does not need to touch at all — #1361's staged-block read path is orthogonal to the drain loop; it only needs the `StagingStore` seam and `sync/staging.rs` helpers, not `drain.rs` itself.

**They should NOT be one PR.** They fix different mechanisms:

**Verdict: VALID**, and the exposure widened with PR #1550.

```rust
        .children(parent)
        .into_iter()
        .find(|child| collation_key(child.name()) == key)
        .map(node_attrs)
```

- Deeper cause found during verification: durable state normally cannot hold two same-fold-key siblings — `Snapshot::name_taken` and `resolve_name` (`crates/engine/src/sync/rebase.rs:774-800`, `crates/engine/src/sync/model.rs:390-396`) auto-suffix a colliding create at rebase time, and a test proves it (`rebase.rs`, "distinct collation keys, no shadowed sibling", around line 1244). But the **optimistic pending-op overlay** does not run this check. `apply_one`'s `OpKind::Create` branch (`crates/engine/src/sync/overlay.rs:33-42`) upserts the new `NodeMeta` unconditionally — the module comment states it deliberately "never drops, suffixes, or dead-letters." So a locally pending create can render, for a real window, alongside a same-fold-key sibling the render already holds (for example, an owner's confirmed file and a grantee's not-yet-rebased create). During that window, `lookup`'s node-id-ordered `.find()` decides which one a host resolves, arbitrarily.
- `NodeAttrs`, which `lookup` returns, carries no `pending` field, so even a caller that wanted to prefer the confirmed node over the pending one cannot today.

**Minimal fix shape:** give `EngineView::lookup` (and `lookup_exact`) a deterministic tiebreak that prefers a confirmed node over one still in the pending overlay when both fold-match, rather than a NodeId-order first-match. This likely needs the overlay or the lookup layer to know which candidate is pending, since `NodeAttrs` today carries no such marker.

**Also relevant:** `crates/fuse/src/ops.rs` (`resolve`), `crates/fuse/src/adapters/windows.rs` (new adapter that removes the junk-only fallback boundary).
**Size: M** (1 day) — the lookup-side change is small, but a correct fix needs a pending/confirmed signal threaded from the overlay through to `NodeAttrs`, plus new tests for the overlay-collision window across at least one case-insensitive adapter path.</result>

## ISSUE #1085 — Placement does not re-decide during a session

**Verdict: VALID.**

**Write and clear points in `Engine::start`, `crates/engine/src/facade.rs`:**
- Write at start: line 3051, `*self.placement.borrow_mut() = Some(decide_placement(&settings));` (after `load_settings` at lines 3040-3050).
- Clear at park/pause: lines 3245-3246, inside `pause()` (or the equivalent stop path).
- Clear on failed start: line 3516, inside `clear_failed_start`.
- Write on a save: line 5694, `save_vault_settings` sets `self.placement` again, but only for a save this session itself makes.

**Resolve tick clone:**
- Line 3744: `let placement = self.placement.clone();` — this `Rc` clone happens once, when the tick loop spawns.
- Line 3784: each pass reads `placement.borrow().clone()` and takes the decision as is. No pass calls `decide_placement` again.
- `DrainScope.placement` (drain.rs:413) is `&'a PlacementDecision`, fixed for the whole pass.

**`load_settings` and fail-closed rule, `crates/engine/src/settings.rs`:**
- `load_settings`: lines 726-773. It resolves the live record, and on a miss or a timeout falls to the cached last-known-good body (`SettingsLoad::Stale`, lines 767-770) and only then to `SettingsLoad::Defaults` (line 771).
- `SettingsLoad` enum: lines 535-550. `Stale` carries the real `settings` plus a `reason`.
- `decide_placement`: lines 422-435. The doc comment at lines 416-421 states the rule directly: only `DefaultsReason::UnprovenFirstRun` still authorizes `Hosted`; every other degraded reason with no cached copy refuses. `Resolved` and `Stale` both route through `placement_of(settings)` (line 424-426), so a degraded reload never widens `External` to `Hosted` — it keeps the true placement or refuses. The rule holds as written.

**Nothing re-decides placement today:**
```
git log -S "placement" --oneline -15 -- crates/engine/src/facade.rs
ef95dc810 fix: retry a failed first-run mint in-session and stop an assumed placement latching BYO (#1338)
abc9a8d30 feat(engine): give the vault settings write plane a facade caller and a renewal slot (#1298)
e373a8955 feat: wire the pin-provider layer across all three modes (#1072)
```
Wave 16's `#1536` (`9d0af2c39`) does not appear in this list. Its diff to `facade.rs` adds `VaultStorageView`/`QuotaView` (read-back for the settings pane, closing #1503) and `SiweLink`/`UnlinkAuthMethod`. It does not touch the placement write path or the resolve tick. `#1536` did not change this.

**Drain refusal, `crates/engine/src/sync/drain.rs`:**
- `Halt::Unclassified` on a placement refusal that carries no user hold: lines 2457-2461, `self.placement.as_ref().map_err(|refusal| refusal.holds().map_or(Halt::Unclassified, Halt::HeldBySettings))?`.

Because `self.placement` is fixed for the pass, a provider a member revokes mid-session is not detected here at all — the pass either keeps sending to the revoked destination or keeps failing under the placement decided at start, until the session restarts.

**Cheap evidence a fix could use:**
The liveness loop (`spawn_liveness_loop`, facade.rs:3663-3696, cadence `RE_PUT_INTERVAL` = 3600s, `net/liveness.rs:40`) already calls `live_settings_record` (facade.rs:2518-2542) every hour. That function does a `fanout_get_verify` on the settings name and compares `live.value != held.value.record_value()` — a cheap, already-paid signal that the settings record moved. Today it only clears the local `settings_record` renewal slot; it never re-decodes the body or re-runs `decide_placement`. A fix could hang the re-decide off this existing hourly check (decode the new body, call `decide_placement`, update `self.placement` and `self.settings_summary`) rather than add a new poll. ## ISSUE #1451 — Preserved dead letters lack durable identity and a discard/recover surface

**Verdict: VALID, and the gap is wider than the title states.**

**Durable preserved set, `crates/engine/src/sync/staging.rs`:**
- Key: line 100, `pub(crate) const PRESERVED_DEAD_LETTERS_KEY: &[u8] = b"cipherbox/preserved-dead-letters";`.
- Format tag: line 104, `const PRESERVED_FORMAT_V2: u8 = 2;`.
- Record type: lines 106-114:
```rust
pub(crate) struct PreservedDeadLetter {
    preserved_at: UnixMillis,
    record: Vec<u8>,
}
```
There is no `OpId` field and no separate identity field of any kind. Identity, if it exists, is only whatever the raw `record` bytes carry internally, and callers key entries by decoding `record_content_root_cid(&entry.record)`, not by any id (see `reconcile_preserved_dead_letters`, staging.rs:579-619, and `orphan_staging_keys`, staging.rs:646 onward).
- Reader/writer: `read_preserved_dead_letters` (staging.rs:412) and `write_preserved_dead_letters` (staging.rs:449).

**A format-v2 change:** a durable identity field would need a new format tag (`PRESERVED_FORMAT_V3` or similar), a codec change in both `read_preserved_dead_letters`/`write_preserved_dead_letters`, and a decision on the `Preservation::Refused` arm (staging.rs:192-198, 242-244) for entries a build cannot parse under the new tag.

**In-memory notice map, `crates/engine/src/facade.rs`:**
- Type: line 2478, `type RetainedDeadLetters = BTreeMap<OpId, (Option<NodeId>, DeadLetterReason)>`.
- Field: line 2829, `dead_letters: Rc<RefCell<RetainedDeadLetters>>`.
- Constructed empty at every `Engine` build: line 2959, `Rc::new(RefCell::new(BTreeMap::new()))`.
- Populated only two ways: (1) at boot, from undecodable queue entries only (lines 3405-3430); (2) live, from a drain pass's own report (`surface_drain_report`, lines 2298-2310, fed by `report.dead_letters.push` at `sync/drain.rs:3065`).

**Confirmed empty on boot and never rehydrated from the durable preserved set:** `PRESERVED_DEAD_LETTERS_KEY` and `read_preserved_dead_letters` do not appear anywhere in `facade.rs` or `crates/engine/src/sync/boot.rs`. A dead letter that reaches `Preservation::Kept` (a version parked past the durable queue, with `ContentUnrecoverable`/`PreservationRefused` reasons among the four `DeadLetterReason` variants, `sync/rebase.rs:98`) surfaces on the event stream once, at the moment it dead-letters. After the next app restart, the host has no way to enumerate it again — its bytes stay durable and protected from orphan GC, but its presence is invisible. This is a stronger gap than "no discard/recover command": there is no durable, boot-stable read surface either.

**Command boilerplate cost for one new command** (using `SiweLink`/`UnlinkAuthMethod` from #1536 as the template):
1. `Command` variant + `name()` arm — `crates/engine/src/facade.rs` (enum ~line 698 onward, `name()` ~line 905 onward).
2. Dispatch arm in the big `match command` — `crates/engine/src/facade.rs:4116` onward.
3. Handler method on `Engine`.
4. Wasm host binding — `crates/wasm/src/lib.rs`, one `~8`-line builder function (pattern at lines 1420-1610, e.g. `UnlinkAuthMethod` at line 1598).
5. Client protocol — `packages/client/src/worker/protocol.ts`, one `CommandDescriptor` variant (lines 315-356).
6. Command codec case — `packages/client/src/worker/commandCodec.ts`, one `case` arm (lines 243-322).
7. No tray hook exists today (`apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/tray.rs` has no dead-letter references); the Tauri engine layer (`apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/engine/mod.rs`) only special-cases `Logout`/`ForgetDevice`/`ManualRefresh` — other commands pass through generically, so a tray action is not required boilerplate unless the product wants one.

So one new command costs roughly 6 sites across 4 files, each small — cheap per command, but this issue wants two (discard, recover) plus the durable identity change underneath both.

**#1524 baseline** (`aa58d7853`, `git log --oneline -20 -- crates/engine/src/sync/drain.rs`): fixed `Preservation::Refused` reporting (an unparseable preserved blob now surfaces `DeadLetterReason::PreservationRefused` instead of silently freezing the queue), fixed a restored-directory replay refusal, and added `reclaim_stalls` reporting. It did **not** add any identity field, any discard/recover command, or any boot-time rehydration of the preserved set into the host view. #1451 starts from that point with the gap fully open.

**Size: M/L.** The durable format bump touches the codec and every reader of `entry.record` across `staging.rs` (reconcile, orphan GC), needs a migration path for existing v2-format installs, needs boot-time rehydration into `dead_letters` (or a parallel durable-backed view), plus two new commands end to end (facade, wasm, protocol.ts, commandCodec.ts) and new tests for discard/recover/boot-persistence.

## ISSUE #1537 — Reclamation drop strands a diamond child in the snapshot

**Verdict: VALID and narrow — a real gap, but small.**

**`settle_reclamation`, `crates/engine/src/sync/drain.rs:1702-1743`, the loop at lines 1726-1738:**
```rust
let mut held = self.held.borrow_mut();
let mut base = self.base.borrow_mut();
for (node, _) in &reclamation.doomed {
    if !base.links_to(*node).is_empty() {
        continue;
    }
    held.remove(&HeldKey::node(node.0));
    held.remove(&HeldKey::scope_pointer(node.0));
    base.remove_node(*node);
}
```
The `links_to` guard (line 1729) correctly skips a doomed node another link still names. But the removal itself, `base.remove_node(*node)` (line 1737), is the shallow form: it drops the node and its own links only. It does not cascade to descendants that lose their last incoming link as a result.

**`Snapshot::remove_node` and `Snapshot::remove_unreachable`, `crates/engine/src/sync/model.rs`:**
- `remove_node` (lines 228-235): shallow, doc comment says so directly — "a node going away for good wants `remove_deleted`".
- `remove_unreachable` (lines 237-258):
```rust
pub fn remove_unreachable(&mut self, id: NodeId) {
    let mut pending = vec![id];
    while let Some(node) = pending.pop() {
        if node == self.root || self.links.iter().any(|l| l.child == node) {
            continue;
        }
        let orphaned: Vec<NodeId> = self.links.iter()
            .filter(|l| l.parent == node).map(|l| l.child).collect();
        self.remove_node(node);
        pending.extend(orphaned);
    }
}
```
Confirmed: it applies exactly the "another link still names it" test (`self.links.iter().any(|l| l.child == node)`) and cascades to a node's own children once that node is removed. It returns `()` — it reports nothing about which ids it dropped.

**Every production caller of `remove_node` outside `model.rs`:**
```
crates/engine/src/sync/rebase.rs:1989   base.remove_node(id(3));   -- inside a #[test] fn only
crates/engine/src/sync/drain.rs:1737    base.remove_node(*node);   -- settle_reclamation, production
```
`settle_reclamation` is the only production caller left. Every other call site in `model.rs` itself now goes through `remove_unreachable`/`remove_deleted`. `remove_node` can be narrowed to `pub(crate)` (or made private to `model.rs` with a thin cascading wrapper exposed instead) without breaking anything outside the test in `rebase.rs`.

**`held`:** `pub(crate) held: &'a RefCell<HeldRecords>` on `DrainScope` (drain.rs:429), the same map as `Engine::held_records` (facade.rs:2775, `Rc<RefCell<HeldRecords>>`). It is pruned in `settle_reclamation` itself (drain.rs:1732, 1736, for the doomed node only) and in the pointer-liveness sweep (facade.rs:2575-2581). No path prunes `held` for a cascaded descendant `remove_unreachable` would drop, since `remove_unreachable` reports no ids today.

**`project_folder`, `crates/engine/src/sync/project.rs:50-92`:** confirmed at lines 64-74 — the observed-remote-delete direction already does this correctly:
```rust
for id in departed {
    snapshot.unlink(folder, id);
    snapshot.remove_unreachable(id);
}
```
This is the pattern `settle_reclamation` should mirror but does not.

**#1512 and #1522, `git log --oneline --grep`:**
- `#1512` does not appear anywhere in the commit history (no hits besides unrelated hash-substring noise).
- `#1522` does appear: `9ba0047a6 fix: cascade the move-replace vacate and fold case fully (#1540)`, which states "Closes #1522." Its own body confirms the same bug class: "Both vacate sites kept the shallow `Snapshot::remove_node`, which left the replaced folder's subtree present but reachable from nothing." The fix changed `Snapshot::relocate` (model.rs:286-297) to call `remove_deleted` (which itself calls `remove_unreachable`) instead of `remove_node`.
- A closely related fix, `b30e2a937` (#1511, "journal what a delete owes at unlink-ack and prune what an observed one detaches"), is what added both the `links_to` guard to `settle_reclamation` and the cascade to `project_folder`. Its own commit body says the local-drop loop "was unconditional... a node a surviving parent also names was dropped from the held set" — this is the guard now at drain.rs:1729. But #1511's fix did not swap `remove_node` for the cascading form inside `settle_reclamation`; it only added the guard.

So the pattern — shallow `remove_node` stranding a subtree — has been fixed twice already (#1511 for `project_folder`'s observed-remote path, #1522/#1540 for the move-replace vacate path) but the third site, `settle_reclamation`, is the one instance still using the shallow form. `#1512` as stated does not correspond to any landed commit; treat it as either a typo for `#1511` or a still-open ticket — it is not evidence this site is already fixed.

**Size: confirm XS/S.** The minimal fix is a one-line swap (`remove_node` → `remove_unreachable`) plus a diamond-child regression test. A complete fix that also avoids stranding `held` entries for cascaded descendants needs `remove_unreachable` to report the ids it drops (a small signature change, two trivial call-site updates in `project.rs:73` and `model.rs:269` to ignore the new return), and `settle_reclamation` to prune `held` for each. That is still small and contained to `drain.rs` + `model.rs`. **S.**

- Line 3744: `let placement = self.placement.clone();` — this `Rc` clone happens once, when the tick loop spawns.
- Line 3784: each pass reads `placement.borrow().clone()` and takes the decision as is. No pass calls `decide_placement` again.

**`load_settings` and fail-closed rule, `crates/engine/src/settings.rs`:**
- `load_settings`: lines 726-773. It resolves the live record, and on a miss or a timeout falls to the cached last-known-good body (`SettingsLoad::Stale`, lines 767-770) and only then to `SettingsLoad::Defaults` (line 771).
- `SettingsLoad` enum: lines 535-550. `Stale` carries the real `settings` plus a `reason`.
- `decide_placement`: lines 422-435. The doc comment at lines 416-421 states the rule directly: only `DefaultsReason::UnprovenFirstRun` still authorizes `Hosted`; every other degraded reason with no cached copy refuses. `Resolved` and `Stale` both route through `placement_of(settings)` (line 424-426), so a degraded reload never widens `External` to `Hosted` — it keeps the true placement or refuses.
```
git log -S "placement" --oneline -15 -- crates/engine/src/facade.rs
ef95dc810 fix: retry a failed first-run mint in-session and stop an assumed placement latching BYO (#1338)
abc9a8d30 feat(engine): give the vault settings write plane a facade caller and a renewal slot (#1298)
e373a8955 feat: wire the pin-provider layer across all three modes (#1072)
```
Wave 16's `#1536` (`9d0af2c39`) does not appear in this list. Its diff to `facade.rs` adds `VaultStorageView`/`QuotaView` (read-back for the settings pane, closing #1503) and `SiweLink`/`UnlinkAuthMethod`. It does not touch the placement write path or the resolve tick. `#1536` did not change this.

## ISSUE #1451 — Preserved dead letters lack durable identity and a discard/recover surface

**Verdict: VALID, and the gap is wider than the title states.**

**Durable preserved set, `crates/engine/src/sync/staging.rs`:**
- Key: line 100, `pub(crate) const PRESERVED_DEAD_LETTERS_KEY: &[u8] = b"cipherbox/preserved-dead-letters";`.
- Format tag: line 104, `const PRESERVED_FORMAT_V2: u8 = 2;`.
- Record type: lines 106-114:
```rust
pub(crate) struct PreservedDeadLetter {
    preserved_at: UnixMillis,
    record: Vec<u8>,
}
```
There is no `OpId` field and no separate identity field of any kind. Identity, if it exists, is only whatever the raw `record` bytes carry internally, and callers key entries by decoding `record_content_root_cid(&entry.record)`, not by any id (see `reconcile_preserved_dead_letters`, staging.rs:579-619, and `orphan_staging_keys`, staging.rs:646 onward).
- Reader/writer: `read_preserved_dead_letters` (staging.rs:412) and `write_preserved_dead_letters` (staging.rs:449).

**A format-v2 change:** a durable identity field would need a new format tag (`PRESERVED_FORMAT_V3` or similar), a codec change in both `read_preserved_dead_letters`/`write_preserved_dead_letters`, and a decision on the `Preservation::Refused` arm (staging.rs:192-198, 242-244) for entries a build cannot parse under the new tag.

**In-memory notice map, `crates/engine/src/facade.rs`:**
- Type: line 2478, `type RetainedDeadLetters = BTreeMap<OpId, (Option<NodeId>, DeadLetterReason)>`.
- Field: line 2829, `dead_letters: Rc<RefCell<RetainedDeadLetters>>`.
- Constructed empty at every `Engine` build: line 2959, `Rc::new(RefCell::new(BTreeMap::new()))`.
- Populated only two ways: (1) at boot, from undecodable queue entries only (lines 3405-3430); (2) live, from a drain pass's own report (`surface_drain_report`, lines 2298-2310, fed by `report.dead_letters.push` at `sync/drain.rs:3065`).

**Confirmed empty on boot and never rehydrated from the durable preserved set:** `PRESERVED_DEAD_LETTERS_KEY` and `read_preserved_dead_letters` do not appear anywhere in `facade.rs` or `crates/engine/src/sync/boot.rs`. A dead letter that reaches `Preservation::Kept` (a version parked past the durable queue, with `ContentUnrecoverable`/`PreservationRefused` reasons among the four `DeadLetterReason` variants, `sync/rebase.rs:98`) surfaces on the event stream once, at the moment it dead-letters. After the next app restart, the host has no way to enumerate it again — its bytes stay durable and protected from orphan GC, but its presence is invisible. This is a stronger gap than "no discard/recover command": there is no durable, boot-stable read surface either.

**Command boilerplate cost for one new command** (using `SiweLink`/`UnlinkAuthMethod` from #1536 as the template):
1. `Command` variant + `name()` arm — `crates/engine/src/facade.rs` (enum ~line 698 onward, `name()` ~line 905 onward).
2. Dispatch arm in the big `match command` — `crates/engine/src/facade.rs:4116` onward.
3. Handler method on `Engine`.
4. Wasm host binding — `crates/wasm/src/lib.rs`, one `~8`-line builder function (pattern at lines 1420-1610, e.g. `UnlinkAuthMethod` at line 1598).
5. Client protocol — `packages/client/src/worker/protocol.ts`, one `CommandDescriptor` variant (lines 315-356).
6. Command codec case — `packages/client/src/worker/commandCodec.ts`, one `case` arm (lines 243-322).
7. No tray hook exists today (`apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/tray.rs` has no dead-letter references); the Tauri engine layer (`apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/engine/mod.rs`) only special-cases `Logout`/`ForgetDevice`/`ManualRefresh` — other commands pass through generically, so a tray action is not required boilerplate unless the product wants one.

So one new command costs roughly 6 sites across 4 files, each small — cheap per command, but this issue wants two (discard, recover) plus the durable identity change underneath both.

**#1524 baseline** (`aa58d7853`, `git log --oneline -20 -- crates/engine/src/sync/drain.rs`): fixed `Preservation::Refused` reporting (an unparseable preserved blob now surfaces `DeadLetterReason::PreservationRefused` instead of silently freezing the queue), fixed a restored-directory replay refusal, and added `reclaim_stalls` reporting. It did **not** add any identity field, any discard/recover command, or any boot-time rehydration of the preserved set into the host view. #1451 starts from that point with the gap fully open.

## ISSUE #1537 — Reclamation drop strands a diamond child in the snapshot

**Verdict: VALID and narrow — a real gap, but small.**

**`settle_reclamation`, `crates/engine/src/sync/drain.rs:1702-1743`, the loop at lines 1726-1738:**
```rust
let mut held = self.held.borrow_mut();
let mut base = self.base.borrow_mut();
for (node, _) in &reclamation.doomed {
    if !base.links_to(*node).is_empty() {
        continue;
    }
    held.remove(&HeldKey::node(node.0));
    held.remove(&HeldKey::scope_pointer(node.0));
    base.remove_node(*node);
}
```
The `links_to` guard (line 1729) correctly skips a doomed node another link still names. But the removal itself, `base.remove_node(*node)` (line 1737), is the shallow form: it drops the node and its own links only. It does not cascade to descendants that lose their last incoming link as a result.

**`Snapshot::remove_node` and `Snapshot::remove_unreachable`, `crates/engine/src/sync/model.rs`:**
- `remove_node` (lines 228-235): shallow, doc comment says so directly — "a node going away for good wants `remove_deleted`".
- `remove_unreachable` (lines 237-258):
```rust
pub fn remove_unreachable(&mut self, id: NodeId) {
    let mut pending = vec![id];
    while let Some(node) = pending.pop() {
        if node == self.root || self.links.iter().any(|l| l.child == node) {
            continue;
        }
        let orphaned: Vec<NodeId> = self.links.iter()
            .filter(|l| l.parent == node).map(|l| l.child).collect();
        self.remove_node(node);
        pending.extend(orphaned);
    }
}
```
Confirmed: it applies exactly the "another link still names it" test (`self.links.iter().any(|l| l.child == node)`) and cascades to a node's own children once that node is removed. It returns `()` — it reports nothing about which ids it dropped.

**Every production caller of `remove_node` outside `model.rs`:**
```
crates/engine/src/sync/rebase.rs:1989   base.remove_node(id(3));   -- inside a #[test] fn only
crates/engine/src/sync/drain.rs:1737    base.remove_node(*node);   -- settle_reclamation, production
```
`settle_reclamation` is the only production caller left. Every other call site in `model.rs` itself now goes through `remove_unreachable`/`remove_deleted`. `remove_node` can be narrowed to `pub(crate)` (or made private to `model.rs` with a thin cascading wrapper exposed instead) without breaking anything outside the test in `rebase.rs`.

**`held`:** `pub(crate) held: &'a RefCell<HeldRecords>` on `DrainScope` (drain.rs:429), the same map as `Engine::held_records` (facade.rs:2775, `Rc<RefCell<HeldRecords>>`). It is pruned in `settle_reclamation` itself (drain.rs:1732, 1736, for the doomed node only) and in the pointer-liveness sweep (facade.rs:2575-2581). No path prunes `held` for a cascaded descendant `remove_unreachable` would drop, since `remove_unreachable` reports no ids today.

**`project_folder`, `crates/engine/src/sync/project.rs:50-92`:** confirmed at lines 64-74 — the observed-remote-delete direction already does this correctly:
```rust
for id in departed {
    snapshot.unlink(folder, id);
    snapshot.remove_unreachable(id);
}
```
This is the pattern `settle_reclamation` should mirror but does not.

**#1512 and #1522, `git log --oneline --grep`:**
- `#1512` does not appear anywhere in the commit history (no hits besides unrelated hash-substring noise).
- `#1522` does appear: `9ba0047a6 fix: cascade the move-replace vacate and fold case fully (#1540)`, which states "Closes #1522." Its own body confirms the same bug class: "Both vacate sites kept the shallow `Snapshot::remove_node`, which left the replaced folder's subtree present but reachable from nothing." The fix changed `Snapshot::relocate` (model.rs:286-297) to call `remove_deleted` (which itself calls `remove_unreachable`) instead of `remove_node`.
- A closely related fix, `b30e2a937` (#1511, "journal what a delete owes at unlink-ack and prune what an observed one detaches"), is what added both the `links_to` guard to `settle_reclamation` and the cascade to `project_folder`. Its own commit body says the local-drop loop "was unconditional... a node a surviving parent also names was dropped from the held set" — this is the guard now at drain.rs:1729. But #1511's fix did not swap `remove_node` for the cascading form inside `settle_reclamation`; it only added the guard.

So the pattern — shallow `remove_node` stranding a subtree — has been fixed twice already (#1511 for `project_folder`'s observed-remote path, #1522/#1540 for the move-replace vacate path) but the third site, `settle_reclamation`, is the one instance still using the shallow form. `#1512` as stated does not correspond to any landed commit; treat it as either a typo for `#1511` or a still-open ticket — it is not evidence this site is already fixed.

**Size: confirm XS/S.** The minimal fix is a one-line swap (`remove_node` → `remove_unreachable`) plus a diamond-child regression test. A complete fix that also avoids stranding `held` entries for cascaded descendants needs `remove_unreachable` to report the ids it drops (a small signature change, two trivial call-site updates in `project.rs:73` and `model.rs:269` to ignore the new return), and `settle_reclamation` to prune `held` for each. That is still small and contained to `drain.rs` + `model.rs`. **S.**

=================== wave17-recon-engine-a.md
## 4. Decisions the user must make

**D1 — #1529: drop the carried `unknown` at re-seal?**
Options: (a) drop `unknown` on re-sealed ledger rows and child-scope refs and bound a carried history
link's `sealed`; (b) keep the carry and raise the budget. (a) also requires retiring the opposing pin
`the_re_mint_carries_each_grants_preserved_unknown_fields_forward` (`net/rotation.rs:6183`).
**Recommend (a).** A rotation is not a republish and owes no byte stability
(FSM1/cipher-box-next#27 D10), and (b) cannot work — the per-item size is attacker-chosen, so no
fixed budget bounds it. Blocks lane R.

**D2 — #1530: how to stop the descendant-local cut replay?**
Options: (a) a durable per-scope revocation floor the engine keeps and the cascade consults —
engine-only, no wire change, no KAT; (b) an epoch or monotonic counter inside the grant-set
commitment — a `crates/core` wire change with KAT impact. Separately, the over-cut: scope the carry
to descendants whose own commitment does not independently attest the recipient, or accept it in
`CONTEXT.md`.
**Recommend (a) plus scoping the carry.** (b) is the cleaner root-cause fix but it is a frozen-wire
change late in the wave; (a) closes the same replay with local durable state the floor law already
models. Blocks lane R, and decides whether #1530 stays an L or becomes an XL.

**D3 — #771: pin the grantee's `write_epoch` to 1, or document the inherited epoch?**
#1547 changed the answer's weight: a write grant now draws a fresh `writeScopeSeed`, so the granted
scope's write plane really is new, which argues for pinning 1. The counter-argument is the durable
write-epoch floor the cut advances — pinning 1 must not collide with a floor already raised for that
scope id.
**Recommend: pin `write_epoch = 1` and assert it**, unless the floor check refutes it, in which case
document. Either way it is one line plus one test in lane F1.

**D4 — #1369: bind `scope_id` into the signed preimage, or derive it at the gate?**
The brief says the user already chose derive-at-gate.
**Recommend confirming that choice.** Option 1 is a `crates/core` wire change plus a KAT
regeneration, which is XL and out of proportion to a `pub(super)` gate with consistent callers.

**D5 — #1548: seal the fragment after the cut, or accept a superseded name?**
Option 1 (seal after the cut, re-mint the tag at the moved name) keeps every comparison exact but
inverts the mint's record-before-publish order. Option 2 is cheaper but widens a trust comparison and
then needs the superseded name proven against the scope pointer.
**Recommend option 1**, which the issue itself prefers — and it is the same re-ordering D6 needs, so
one change buys both.

**D6 — #1549: resumable cut, or post the share pointer after the cut?**
**Recommend option 2 first** (post the pointer after the cut), landed together with D5's re-order. It
is the smaller change, matches the blueprint's stated order, and narrows the window to "the grantee
never learns of a scope that exists". File option 1's start-up reconciliation as a separate
`post-cutover` issue if the residual is judged acceptable.

**D7 — #857: retire the shared zero root scope id, or keep it?**
**Recommend: keep the constant, and close #857 with the finding.** Evidence in section 2: every KDF
that consumes `root_scope_id` also consumes `login_secret` or the owner identity, so the constant is
a well-known anchor and account separation already lives elsewhere. The one genuine cross-account
surface is `FloorStore`'s raw-`scope_id` key (`seams/floor_store.rs:29-42`), which is exactly what
#1345 part 2 must fix anyway. **Do not give it a wave slot** — fold the answer into lane G's PR.

**D8 — #1345 part 2: what key replaces the sharer-authored scope id at the floor?**
Options: (a) bind `(sharer_identity_pk, scope_id)` at the accept path before any advance; (b)
namespace the whole `FloorStore` per account. (a) is local to `grants/accept.rs` +
`gate/adoption.rs`; (b) is a seam change that also answers D7 structurally.
**Recommend (a)** for the wave, and record (b) as the shape D7 would have taken. Blocks lane G.

**D9 — #1531 scope:** the body also proposes resizing the 42% root-rest reservation from the

content.text:
The wallet sign-in stays in scope. The issue is about two routes that accept the same signed SIWE message:

| Route | Returns | Callers on main |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /auth/identity/wallet` | an identity token → Core Kit derives the account key (ADR 0008) | web wallet button (`WalletLoginButton.tsx:14-30`), `packages/login/src/identity.ts:88`, the e2e login page object (`login.page.ts:16` → `wallet-login-button`), `smoke.spec.ts:12` |
| `POST /auth/siwe/login` | a session on an already-linked wallet | only the engine `Command::SiweLogin` (`facade.rs:4270`, `api/client.rs:195`). No UI, no e2e, no desktop reference, no line in `blueprint/api.md`. |

So the e2e suite depends on wallet sign-in through `/auth/identity/wallet`, and that route is not touched. "Delete" in #1545 means: remove only `/auth/siwe/login`, `ApiClient::siwe_login`, and `Command::SiweLogin`. The wallet button, the nonce mint (`/auth/siwe/challenge`), the link routes (`/auth/siwe/link*`), and every e2e path keep their behavior.

The risk the issue fixes: one signed message can be replayed at either route, and the two differ in strength. With one route left, the pair cannot be confused.

If you want `/auth/siwe/login` kept as a future product surface (a session without a key derivation), the answer is "split" instead: a new nonce kind `siwe-identity`, its own statement, its own mint. That costs an S in `apps/api` + `packages/login` + the web statement copy.

Recommendation stands: delete. Do you confirm delete, or split?
